page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is an entry-tier compute instance belonging to the low-memory variant of the Dlsv7 series. Built on the x86_64 architecture and virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the machine is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Hardware provisioning allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is configured at 4.0 GB total (2.0 GB per vCPU), backed by an expansive 480 MB L3 cache on the host chip. The instance features modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote network-attached disks for persistence. In synthetic and computational benchmarks, the high clock speed enables top-tier single-core execution, highlighted by strong single-core scores in Geekbench and resilient text processing capability. However, with only a single underlying physical core and 4.0 GB of memory, overall throughput drops significantly in multi-threaded scenarios. Multi-core Geekbench metrics, software compilation tasks, and database transactional performance test in the bottom tier relative to broader cloud baselines.

Architecturally, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a lean compute profile where cost efficiency is realized for tasks that benefit from burstable or per-thread CPU clock frequencies without demanding dense memory footprints. The primary tradeoff lies in the restricted aggregate memory bandwidth and low thread count, rendering the instance constrained under concurrency. Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is best fitted for small-scale web serving, microservices, utility scripts, light CI/CD workers, and text-based preprocessing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is a compact, compute-focused virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical core and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Modern vector extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, are supported. The instance includes neither bundled local storage nor GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage. Benchmark data reflects top-tier single-core performance, making it well-suited for single-threaded processing and small-footprint workloads. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth register at the lower end of benchmark baselines due to the single-core constraint. Cost efficiency is centered on workloads that require strong clock speeds without excessive RAM allocation, such as microservices, lightweight web servers, and modest CI/CD pipeline workers.
